source.title: Characterizing Universal Object Representations Across Vision Models
source.authors: Florian P. Mahner; Johannes Roth; Ka-Chun Lam; Michael F. Bonner; Francisco Pereira; M. Hebart

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures recurring representational dimensions across vision models, but uses a factorization-and-matching method rather than the original studies’ methods. It also tests whether universality tracks model size and accuracy and checks robustness to input sets and similarity metrics.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many results directly about cross-model universality, its relationship to size and accuracy, the content of recurring dimensions, and robustness checks. Results cited from other work are not recorded. Human-rating reliability and factorization implementation details are omitted where they do not independently measure a claim version.
record.test_reason: The study measures recurring object-similarity dimensions across 162 vision models with a new method (symmetric NMF plus null-adjusted Hungarian matching). It checks whether universality tracks size and accuracy (V1), whether it is complete or explained by objective or data (V7), whether recurring dimensions are interpretable (V5), and whether rankings survive changes of image set, metric and rank (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also argue that universal dimensions likely reflect the visual world itself, given their alignment with IT and human judgments. They call universality an emergent property of successful visual representation learning, even though it is uncorrelated with ImageNet accuracy. They stress that convergence is far from complete.
record.recipe_differences: Uses penultimate-layer representations to form RBF object-similarity matrices, decomposes them with symmetric NMF, and measures recurring dimensions using null-adjusted one-to-one matching. It does not use the original studies’ methods for convergence or test convergence increasing along a controlled scale sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The model ranking was largely preserved when using ObjectNet (ρ = 0.81), subsampling models (median ρ = 0.97), excluding architecture families (ρ = 0.83), and changing rank from 50 to 10, 30, or 100 (ρ at least 0.93; rank 200 was an exception). Rankings also correlated with CKA (ρ = 0.89); dimension scores correlated with a ridge-regression proxy (ρ = 0.82).

fits_no_version.finding: Models with more universal dimensions predict macaque IT activity (r=0.74) and human odd-one-out judgments (r=0.76) better; the universal half of each model's dimensions beats the specific half (0.42 vs 0.37 triplet accuracy).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dimensions that recur across vision models are the ones most aligned with biological vision and human similarity judgments.

fits_no_version.finding: Among ImageNet-1K classifiers, architecture class (CNN/ViT/Mixer/hybrid) has no significant effect on universality (p=0.33).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model universality of representational dimensions is not tied to architecture class.

record.problems: The paper does not run a controlled scale or compute sweep; size and accuracy are correlational checks. Universality depends on a chosen representation decomposition and primarily penultimate-layer features. Some task/objective contrasts use small groups, and the rank-200 robustness result is not quantified in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-bearing result was omitted for the row limit. Supplementary participant-label reliability details and factorization optimization diagnostics were not recorded because they do not independently test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: No controlled scale or compute sweep within a model family; size and accuracy are cross-sectional correlations. No cross-modal alignment.
Entirely untested: no image-caption or vision-language alignment.
Entirely untested: the seeds are NMF initializations, not independently trained networks.
Entirely untested: no linear maps, stitching, relative representations or unpaired mapping.
Neurons, SAE features and circuits are not tested; only nonnegative similarity-structure dimensions from the penultimate layer.
Number of neighbours / kNN-type metric settings, other layers, and absolute convergence levels under alternative inputs or metrics are not tested.
Whether a common model of reality causes alignment is not tested, beyond a correlational link to IT and behaviour; no plateau-with-scale analysis.

missing.what: Leave-family-out stability: universality recomputed without same-architecture-family models correlates ρ=0.83 with the full set.
Per-rank Spearman values, including rank 200 ≈0.89, shown in the figure panels.
Within-model stability ceiling distribution: median 0.84, IQR [0.75, 0.90]; the authors call it a liberal upper bound.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source is this study. The V1 challenge rests on cross-sectional correlations within a heterogeneous vision-only zoo, not a controlled scale series. The V6 evidence concerns stability of model rankings, not invariance of absolute convergence levels. R3 is about stability of the model set, not V6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not sweep model scale, training compute, or capability over a controlled model series; does not test cross-modal alignment or convergence across independently trained versions of the same model.
No paired image-caption representation alignment or vision-language model performance trend is tested.
The five random initializations are NMF factorization runs, not independently trained networks; no shared-feature or shared-subspace result across training seeds is reported.
No representation mapping, layer stitching, relative representation, or unpaired mapping is evaluated.
Tests recurring nonnegative dimensions of object-similarity structure and their human-rated content, not recurrence of individual neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

Tests ObjectNet versus THINGS, several metric validations, and factorization rank; does not comprehensively vary similarity-measure settings such as neighborhood count or test broad out-of-distribution domains.

Tests whether measured universality is complete and whether selected architecture, objective, and data contrasts account for it; does not establish that a common model of reality causes alignment or comprehensively identify shared training-data/objective causes.

rows.subject: all 162 vision models (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: 162 models; 50 dimensions per model for the main comparisons
rows.stage_stated: pretrained; one untrained baseline is included in the model set
rows.operation_detail: Matched dimensions across models using null-adjusted squared-cosine similarity and one-to-one Hungarian assignment
rows.measure: Per-dimension universality score
rows.baseline: Chance-level agreement is calibrated to near 0; within-model stability ceiling median 0.84
rows.value: Scores ranged from near chance (0.0003) to 0.54; the maximum is 64% of the within-model stability ceiling
rows.note: The authors also report that 80% of models had dimensions in both the top and bottom universality quartiles, indicating both recurring and model-specific dimensions.

source_check.correct: V5: partial recurrence. V7: observed incomplete convergence; scores range from 0.0003 to 0.54, with the maximum reaching 64% of the median within-model ceiling of 0.84.
source_check.problem: The partial state fits the recurrence qualification but should be observed for V7, which explicitly predicts incomplete convergence.

rows.check: ρ=0.81 compares model rankings across THINGS and ObjectNet, not absolute convergence levels. ObjectNet universality levels are not reported, so a drop in level cannot be excluded.

rows.subject: Taskonomy ResNet-50 encoders (aggregate by task cluster)
rows.size_stated: 25 encoders; 23 included in the cluster test after excluding two singleton clusters
rows.stage_stated: trained on different Taskonomy visual tasks
rows.operation_detail: Compared universality across task clusters
rows.measure: Per-dimension universality by task cluster
rows.value: Taskonomy cluster means ranged from 0.05 to 0.12; task cluster effect F(3, 19) = 12.7, p < .001, ω² = 0.60; semantic tasks were highest, followed by 3D, geometric, and 2D tasks
rows.note: The authors attribute the low overall Taskonomy universality relative to the full model set to the narrow distributions of the training tasks.
rows.check: Task objective strongly modulates universality only within the narrow Taskonomy family (cluster means 0.05–0.12). This bears on the 'shared objectives explain it' part of V7 only within that family.

source_check.correct: State: observed for V7 in this condition group. Taskonomy universality is low overall, and task cluster significantly affects universality: F(3,19)=12.7, p<.001, ω²=0.60.
source_check.problem: Low convergence and a strong objective effect instantiate V7 within Taskonomy rather than showing its effect only partially.
